abstract: The rapid growth of predicted RNA structure databases demands fast and sensitive structural search methods. Sequence-based approaches lose sensitivity for divergent homologues, whereas exhaustive coordinate alignment is computationally expensive. Analogous to Foldseeks 3Di representation, we introduce RFoldSearch and 3Dr, a learned 80-state structural alphabet encoding local RNA tertiary environments. RFoldSearch combines indexed prefiltering, structure-aware token alignment and optional coordinate-based reranking. On held-out RNAsolo 2.0 queries, RFoldSearch retained 81-89% of the family-level sensitivity of exhaustive coordinate aligners and outperformed RiboSeek (RS-20) and BLASTN. On a single CPU core, RFoldSearch searched 531,888 predicted structures in 0.31 s per query, 20-fold faster than RiboSeek with its RS-20 alphabet while using 7.7-fold less peak memory. Searches of predicted-structure databases demonstrated its ability to recover structurally similar RNAs with limited detectable sequence similarity, complementing profile-based sequence search. Recurrent 3Dr words captured conserved local RNA geometries, including fragments corresponding to known RNA 3D motifs. RFoldSearch is available as open-source software, a web server and a REST API.
